shortDescription: Framework for entad items: randomly rolled traits by rarity that modify stats, damage, abilities and buildings, stay hidden until revealed, and make every entad more durable by its highest rarity.
body:
## Durability
- Every item with at least one entad trait gets its MaxHitPoints multiplied by `EntadSettings.Durability[highest trait rarity]`. Defaults: Common x1.25, Uncommon x1.5, Rare x2, Epic x3, Legendary x5. Each is adjustable from 1 to 10 in the settings (General tab), and "Reset to defaults" covers them. The multiplier is applied last in `StatPart_Entad.TransformValue` and is never hidden.
- The MaxHitPoints explanation includes "Entad durability (Rarity): xN%", but vanilla's info-card Hit points row never shows stat explanations. The user is fine with that, so it is left as is.
- HP keeps its health fraction:
  - On trait add or remove, via `RescaleHitPoints`. This now runs for every trait, since any trait can change the highest rarity.
  - When the settings window closes mid-game, through `EntadMod.WriteSettings` and `EntadUtility.RescaleDurability`, which walks every map and caravan.
  - On load, through `SyncDurability`. Each comp saves `scaledDurability`, the factor its HP was last scaled to; the default of 1 means a save from before durability existed. A mismatch on load rescales the item, which covers old saves, main-menu settings changes and items the window couldn't reach.
  - A full-health item snaps to the new maximum, with slack for MaxHitPoints' rounding to 5 above 200.
- MaxHitPoints is always injected but stays immutable, keeping vanilla's permanent cache. Every real change calls `ClearCacheForThing`, which also empties the immutable cache.

## Wearer stats (EntadWearerStats.cs)
- Entad trait offsets on pawn stats (IsWearerStat categories) reach the holder through a postfix on `StatWorker.StatOffsetFromGear`. `StatPart_Entad` skips those offsets when it evaluates apparel or equipment, so they aren't counted twice. Buildings still get theirs.
- "Relevant gear": `GearAffectsStat` only sees a ThingDef, so a [ThreadStatic] `explainingPawn` is set around `GetExplanationUnfinalized` and during each MoveNext of `GetInfoCardHyperlinks`. An item is listed when the pawn holds one of that def with a non-zero revealed entad offset.

## Hiding unrevealed traits in displays
Gameplay always applies every trait. Three thread-static flags make the displays leave hidden ones out:
- `displayExcludesHidden`: set during `InfoTextLineFromGear`, the pawn's gear line. Wearer stats only.
- `gearCardThing`: set during `ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats`, the item's equipped-offset rows. Wearer stats only.
- `infoCardThing`: set during `StatsReportUtility.DrawStatsReport(Rect, Thing)`, the whole item info card. Every stat of that item except MaxHitPoints, because the HP row shows real HitPoints / MaxHitPoints. Set only when the item has an unrevealed Stat effect. Tested in-game: a hidden cooldown trait shows the base cooldown on the card.
- Anything computed under `infoCardThing` lands in the stat cache, so the finalizer runs `CompEntad.ClearCardStatCaches()` every frame. That clears the item and its holder for every stat the traits name, plus MarketValue. Derived stats are not cleared; vanilla reads those with cacheStaleAfterTicks -1, so it doesn't matter.
- Market value: hidden traits still count as the flat "unidentified" bonus.

## Startup
- `EntadStatPartInjector` adds `StatPart_Entad` to every stat a trait references, plus MarketValue and MaxHitPoints, and clears `immutable` on those stats except MaxHitPoints. Then it applies each `[HarmonyPatch]` class on its own, each in its own try/catch. Only classes with `[HarmonyPatch]` are processed, because Harmony would otherwise invoke any static `Prepare`.
- Trait add, remove and reveal clear the item's and the holder's stat caches, MaxHitPoints included.

## Performance notes
- `EntadTraitDef.EffectKinds` is cached; it's read by IsRevealed and AnyHidden.
- `CompEntad.WearerOffset` returns early when the item has no traits.
- The flag tables (`AffectsStat`, `IsEntadGearDef`) are index arrays.
- MaxHitPoints keeps its immutable cache. Only the settings-close rescale walks every thing, and only when a durability value changed.

## Open items
- `gearFlags` is a one-time snapshot.
- Def hot-reload doesn't re-run the injector.
- The settings rescale sets HitPoints directly, so a spawned entad building's repair listing isn't refreshed. This is unlikely to matter, since full items stay full.

## Dev tools
- "Add specific Entad trait" lists applicable traits first, then the rest, alphabetically within each group.
